To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the δ13C of soil organic carbon is negatively correlated to mean annual precipitation, and this relationship is robust in the study area.

the negative correlation of the surface soil δ13C with the mean annual precipitation (MAP) is robust and that this relationship can be used to develop a transfer function for reconstructing the paleoclimatological conditions from the isotopic composition of organic carbon in the eolian–paledosol sequences of central-east Asia.

the surface-soil δ13C values are significantly correlated with climatic factors (i.e., mean annual precipitation, mean annual air temperature, and mean annual potential evapotranspiration), and that this correlation can be used to reconstruct paleoclimatic conditions in central-east Asia.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the climatic dependency of soil δ13C values along the S–North Transect in central-east Asia, and the results show that soil δ13C is significantly and negatively related to the mean annual precipitation, and the δ13C values are also significantly and positively correlated with the mean annual temperature.

the development and validation of transfer functions to retrieve the paleoclimate information stored in the eolian–palesol sequences in central-east Asia, which is one of the most arid areas in the world.
the development of a transfer function that can be used in reconstructing the paleoclimates in central-east Asia based on soil organic carbon isotopes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the surface-soil δ13C values in central-east Asia are negatively correlated with mean annual precipitation and the correlation coefficient is 0.453.

the δ13C values of the surface soil organic carbon in central-east Asia are controlled by the mean annual precipitation and the mean annual temperature, with the former being the primary controlling factor.
the soil organic carbon δ13C values are not only controlled by the climate but also affected by other factors such as soil properties and vegetation types.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the δ13C value of surface soil organic matter (SOM) is a good indicator for the mean annual precipitation in central-east Asia, and this relationship can be used to reconstruct the paleoclimate in the past.
the climatic dependency of soil δ13C is a useful tool for the reconstruction of past precipitation in the central-east Asian region.
the climatic dependency of surface-soil organic carbon δ13C values along the S–North transect in central-east Asia is mainly controlled by precipitation and temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the soil organic carbon isotopes in central-east Asia can be used as a reliable proxy of paleoclimate, especially the mean annual precipitation.

the surface-soil δ13C values in central-east Asia are mainly controlled by the mean annual precipitation and the mean annual temperature, with the mean annual precipitation being the main controlling factor.
the δ13C values of the surface soil are a good proxy for the paleoclimate of the past 100,000 years in central-east Asia.
